subject: Re: Request to temporarily extend log retention and DPA addendum
body:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@northstarhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@northstarhealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request to temporarily extend log retention and DPA addendum

Hi Connor,

We have an ongoing internal investigation and our legal team is asking if Redwood can temporarily retain a subset of diagnostic logs and encrypted snapshots for an additional 90 days beyond the standard retention window for the affected tenant (NorthStar Health, account NS-00321). Our DPA (section 5.2) allows for lawful hold but we need a short addendum that: (1) documents the temporary retention window, (2) confirms which subprocessors will have access to backups/snapshots, and (3) provides the expected backup purge timeline and evidence that purges will be irreversible.

Can you confirm what information you can provide and whether Redwood would sign a short addendum? For the evidence, we need:
- the backup purge schedule for the EU and US regions (we're hitting logs in both)
- a list of subprocessors with access to snapshot storage and an indication of whether they are cross-border subprocessors
- any available forensic/export log showing when a purge was executed (or the playbook you run)

I'm attaching a draft addendum and a high-level list of affected endpoints. Please let us know the fastest path — our legal prefers to get this in place before 2026-12-07.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Senior Security Counsel
NorthStar Health

Attachment: DPA_Addendum_NorthStar_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

---

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request to temporarily extend log retention and DPA addendum

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask and the draft addendum. Short answers up front: yes, we can accommodate a 90-day temporary retention hold for the specified tenant; yes, we will provide a signed addendum accepting those terms (subject to a few clarifications); and yes, we can provide a purge evidence artifact on completion.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal (Kimberly) to review your draft and highlight any DPA language we need to adapt (scope, data types, termination).
2) Product/ops (Aditya/Marissa) to confirm the precise slices of logs/snapshots that will be held and create a one-off retention policy tied to the tenant ID.
3) Ops to produce a time-stamped purge report once the 90-day hold expires.

Operational details we need from you:
- Canonical tenant ID(s) and examples of the keys/paths for the snapshots (so we can avoid holding unrelated data)
- Whether you require the hold to include offsite/archived snapshots (we treat offsite cold archives differently)

Kimberly/Aditya/Marissa: looping you in to confirm legal language and the engineering/ops feasibility & timeline.

Connor
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

---

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@northstarhealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request to temporarily extend log retention and DPA addendum

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the draft addendum. I reviewed the PDF and made inline suggestions (mainly: tighten the definition of "logs" vs "snapshots", add a maximum cap on retained volume, and clarify access controls for subprocessors). A couple items for your legal to confirm:
- Proposed hold duration: 90 days from issuance of signed addendum (we prefer a fixed term rather than an open-ended hold).
- Access: Redwood will limit access to named roles and will log access to snapshots; we can provide an access log extract on request, but it will be redacted for internal account identifiers.
- Subprocessors: we list them below with cross-border flags. If NorthStar requires a specific subprocessor restriction, that will need procurement approval.

Subprocessor summary (high level):
- Cloud object storage provider: ArcusCloud (US, EU regions) — stores encrypted snapshots; access is by Redwood-managed service account.
- Long-term cold archive vendor: GlacierSafe (US-only) — used only for >180-day archival; not in scope for a 90-day hold unless specifically requested.
- Backup processing & orchestration: HelixOps (US-based) — handles snapshot coordination; does not have plaintext access to customer payloads.
- Monitoring/alerting: BeaconMetrics (US/EU) — receives hashed telemetry and metadata only.

Aditya / Marissa: can you confirm that we can produce a purge-report (signed timestamped artifact) and the expected timeline to implement a tenant-scoped 90-day retention hold? Also confirm whether offsite cold archives would require additional approvals.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@northstarhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request to temporarily extend log retention and DPA addendum

Elena —

Operational confirmation: we can implement a tenant-scoped retention extension within 48 hours of a signed addendum. Details:
- Scope: diagnostic logs (tokenized metadata, request/response headers) and encrypted snapshots only.
- Exclusions: long-term cold archives stored with GlacierSafe (>180d) are excluded unless you explicitly opt-in.
- Implementation steps (high level):
  1) Legal signs addendum and confirms tenant IDs.
  2) Ops creates a policy object and a temporary retention flag tied to the tenant ID.
  3) We tag current snapshots and mark them "hold:NS-00321-DEC2026"; future snapshots created during the hold will inherit the flag.
  4) At expiry, Ops will run the purge workflow and produce a signed purge-report (PDF) containing: list of objects purged, checksums, timestamps, and the operator's signature.

Purge timeline (examples):
- Standard: automated purge jobs run nightly; for a tenant hold we will run a controlled purge in the first 24 hours after expiry, with a forensics window for evidence collection (we will not re-create purged objects).

Evidence and export options: we can provide:
- Pre-purge snapshot manifest (CSV)
- Signed purge-report (PDF) after purge completes
- Access log extract (CSV) limited to the timeframe of the hold

We will attach a draft internal schedule for the purge process to this thread (see attachment).

Aditya
Senior Product Manager, Data Lifecycle
Redwood Inference

Attachment: backup-purge-schedule-2026Q4.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

---

On Thu, Dec 2, 2026 at 16:03 Elena Torres <elena.torres@northstarhealth.com> wrote:

Connor/Team —

This is perfect and faster than we expected. We will:
- Confirm tenant IDs by EOD tomorrow (2026-12-03).
- Review Kimberly's inline changes and respond with one small tweak around the maximum retained volume.

Pending that, NorthStar is comfortable moving forward with the 90-day fixed hold and we will route the signed addendum through procurement once Kimberly's edits are accepted.

Two quick follow-ups:
1) Will the purge-report include checksums for the purged objects? Our forensics team uses checksums to cross-validate exports.
2) For cross-border artifacts: can you flag objects that moved between US/EU storage during the snapshot window? We may need that for regulatory reporting.

Thanks again — grateful for the quick turnaround.

—Elena
